messages:
Ava (People Ops): @here quick update — rolling out two small but important PTO & travel changes starting today: same-day "auto-approve" for on-call recovery days, and an emergency travel exception path for critical cross-border work. TL;DR: less friction for oncall recovery; a lightweight approval flow for urgent business travel across borders. https://redwood.company/hr/pto-exceptions :sparkles:
Ben (Eng): huge +1. how does auto-approve work for partial-day recovery? e.g., 3 hours after a late pager?
Ava (People Ops): good Q — auto-approve applies to full-day recovery or half-day (>=4 hours). For <4 hours please use the usual time-off request so managers see the exact window. The system will automatically mark the request approved and notify your manager. :white_check_mark:
Sofia (Platform): will this affect payroll or accruals? need to know for shift accounting.
Ava (People Ops): accruals unchanged — it's purely an approval UX change. We still deduct from your PTO balance unless you elect to use the oncall recovery bank (if eligible). We'll show an entry on the payslip as "Recovery PTO" for clarity.
Jamal (Manager): what about retroactive claims? someone covered a 3am incident last week and forgot to file. can we backdate?
Ava (People Ops): managers can retro-approve up to 14 days via the manager portal. After 14 days you'll need People Ops to help — please ping us with the incident link.
Ben (Eng): who gets notified when auto-approved? manager only, or team?
Oncall Bot: Automatic recovery request created for Ben (Eng) — status: auto-approved. Manager Jamal notified.
Eli (Security): travel exception flow — does this include compliance checks for country-specific rules?
Ava (People Ops): yes — the form triggers a quick validation step with Security and Legal for flagged countries. The workflow is: submit emergency travel exception form -> Security/Legal auto-review (within 4 hrs) -> if green, People Ops issues travel waiver and expedition guidance. If not, we'll escalate. Link: `https://redwood.company/forms/emergency-travel`
Ben (Eng): does this cover vaccine/visa docs & expense pre-approval?
Ava (People Ops): vaccine/visa docs are still required where law mandates. Expense pre-approval is optional but recommended for high-cost trips — use `#travel-approvals` for that.
Jamal (Manager): receipts for emergency travel — can employees submit post-trip and still get advance reimbursement?
Ava (People Ops): yes — for approved emergency exceptions we allow post-trip submission within 30 days with manager sign-off. We'll fast-track reimbursements as "priority".
HR Bot: Reminder: submit travel exception using the official form. Missing fields will delay approval.
Sofia (Platform): thanks — can People Ops add a short widget in the Console so teams see status of travel exception reviews?
Ava (People Ops): feature request noted. We'll pilot a simple status card in the Console for the next two-week sprint. If it helps, we're also publishing a one-pager FAQ later today.
Ben (Eng): thx Ava. much appreciated — this should reduce churn on late-night oncall. :raised_hands:
Ava (People Ops): thanks everyone. if you hit any edge cases, DM me or drop a note in `#people-ops`. we'll monitor the first two weeks and iterate. :heart:
